Summary  
Data source overview: The paper surveys limitations of current formal verification techniques for autonomous cyber-physical systems (CPS) and introduces the FOSSIL / FOSSIL⁺ symbolic-reinforcement-learning frameworks. These frameworks couple vision inputs to symbolic states, enforce hybrid-program safety constraints during learning and execution, and use online, verification-preserving program synthesis to repair modelling inaccuracies, with empirical results on the Atari Road Runner domain.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[71] – The main arguments, empirical findings and proposed solutions are represented; node names follow granularity rules and edges reproduce the causal–interventional reasoning given in the text. Small uncertainties remain about implicit causal ordering and the experimental maturity of online program-synthesis components.

Inference strategy justification: Moderate inference (confidence 2) was used only to clarify lifecycle stage and maturity of interventions and to connect FOSSIL⁺’s exploratory results to online program-synthesis mechanisms explicitly advocated by the authors.

Extraction completeness explanation: Every distinct risk–to-intervention pathway in the paper is captured, decomposing the high-level “FOSSIL” idea into white-box component nodes (template mapping, hybrid-program monitors, online synthesis). All nodes are linked; no satellites remain.

Key limitations:  
1) The paper discusses, but does not yet experimentally validate, new vision-system verification tooling; these speculative ideas were omitted to avoid low-confidence paths.  
2) Quantitative edge confidences are approximate because detailed statistical results are sparse.  
3) Some edges cross “non-canonical” category order (e.g. a theoretical insight leading to degraded performance) but were retained to preserve fidelity.
